fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "A homestead collapse that led to the forks", "body": "Carla Adams tells Chance Garton that her path started when she and her husband finally bought land and went off grid, and she found she could not push through anymore. With her children grown, she knew she had to heal old things that had bothered her all her life. Within about thirty days of leaving the homestead she heard an interview with Eileen Day McCusick, learned about tuning forks, and knew immediately that was the work. She landed in what she believes was the last live biofield tuning class before everything shut down for COVID."}, {"title": "Eve, the orbs of light and the restoration group", "body": "Raised in a Christian home, Carla kept turning over what the story of Adam and Eve really meant, and concluded it described a formative mind that believed whatever it was told. She spoke to Eve directly, said it was not her fault, and got a response, an angel and then orbs of light around her. Those, she says, were ancestors carrying the same story. She began tuning them as what she called the restoration group, reasoning that beings made entirely of spirit sit in the same electromagnetic soup we do and need clearing too."}, {"title": "The grandfather who asked for help", "body": "Three or four weeks into tuning that group, Carla's grandfather, dead twenty five years, stood in front of her in her kitchen and said he needed help reaching the oneness. She was frightened, and admits that if it had been anyone else she might have dropped biofield work entirely, since none of this is taught in class. Instead she worked out how to help him across. That opened the systematic project of the book, clearing every named ancestor back four generations and discovering which of their patterns were also sitting inside her."}, {"title": "Nested biofields and where the ancestors live", "body": "Another tuner explained to Carla that past the roughly six or seven foot edge of your own field lies a second field reaching out about thirty five feet, holding the life records of all your ancestors. Asking what came next, she found nature, then the oneness, with the sky clock and a band of concentrated source energy overlapping them. A fifth turned out not to be a container at all but an unending expanse, a void. Chance compares the layered picture to mystery school emanation and offers his own version, wombs all the way down."}, {"title": "Birth stories, inherited grief and the book", "body": "Both agree the formative mind starts at conception, not birth. Carla describes absorbing her parents' stress over an unplanned second pregnancy and blaming herself. Chance recounts tuning his own hologram that day and finding rage at the edge of his field around circumcision and the cord. He tells of two sisters carrying sacral resentment traced to a grandmother abused in a Canadian residential school, the second sister already largely cleared. Carla found her own unexplained sadness belonged to a grandmother who lost her mother and a child. Her book, Ancestral River, and her site ancestralriver.com carry the rest."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Fellow Biofield Tuner, Carla Adams, joins InnerVerse to discuss her new book: Ancestral River: A Spiritual Journey for the Living and the Dead. Join us to learn more about the information our Auras and bodies contain about our biological predecessors, how Biofield Tuning works on our own health and mental state, and what this process can do to help our stuck ancestors transition to the Oneness and assist our journeys instead of hindering us.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Hierarchy That Follows Us Past Death", "body": "Carla describes a control grid of hierarchical leadership operating in the afterlife, run by people who held power while living and who, as she perceives it, were trained along family lines through rituals repeated every five or ten years to lead there too. She insists they hold no real authority over anyone, only the authority we hand them by accepting fear and the belief that we are not enough. Chance adds that the Greek root of demon pointed to deceased human beings rather than innately evil entities, and calls the whole structure demon corp, speculating about astral recruiters who meet frightened people at the point of death."}, {"title": "Inside the Waiting Place", "body": "Carla calls the realm where most souls land the waiting place, a limbo with no tracking of time where beings linger because they lack knowledge or cannot release unsettled emotions. Chance suggests much of the hesitation is fear of retribution, conditioned by how sin, punishment and even action movies frame mistakes. Carla answers that it boils down to learning, noting school taught us to pass tests rather than think. She describes ancestors crossing sometimes by the hundreds, five requirements mirrored in the spiritual chakras, and transitions happening where two ley lines cross at ninety degrees, forming a positive vortex, while graveyards sit on negative ones."}, {"title": "Clearing Ancestors Through the Living", "body": "Carla explains that she does not tune the dead directly, because souls outside the oneness may still carry the mindset of lack, fear and control, and she only wants to trust those aligned with universal spirit. Instead she tunes living clients, clearing the record of their ancestors held within them, which helps the client, the lineage, the practitioner and the whole. Most of her clients know little beyond their grandparents, and she says that knowledge is not needed. Chance marvels at how little modern people know of their own family trees, and Carla describes perceiving ancestors in grayscale, their period clothing a sign of a hierarchical mindset still worn."}, {"title": "Apples, Offers and the Ancient Trees", "body": "Chance offers a flash of philology: with P shifting to F and L to R, the apple of the fall becomes an offer, and he wonders whether the fall meant becoming certain we are only bodies chained to clock time, when pure potential feels like uncertainty. Carla then shares a meditation vision of enormous ancient trees with thick oval leaves that drew crystal vibrations from the earth and broadcast them through the sky, giving everyone a kind of daily tuning. In that era, she was shown, people could choose when to return to the oneness. Chance muses that earlier emanations may have produced fewer, larger beings holding more energy."}, {"title": "Energy Hygiene and Claiming Your Rights", "body": "Asked about closing a session cleanly, Carla says released energy can linger in corners and around ceiling fans, so she first uses her mind to order every dissonant energy out of her home, then sweeps with a small fork. She finishes tunings with upward strikes from the earth star, an approach inspired by Donna Eden's free material. Chance notes that a fork's vibration works like a flashlight in the dark and resolves to clear corners after clients too. He then leads listeners through a group tuning of the spiritual rights from Carla's book, chakra by chakra, using a 384 hertz fork his audience crowdfunded."}]
